userStories.title: Inventory the existing LEAP application
userStories.description: Perform a comprehensive read-only audit of the existing LEAP codebase before making major changes. Identify the application architecture, routes/pages, reusable UI components, API routes, external API integrations, authentication, database access, AI integrations, video/content systems, LaTeX rendering, and critical user flows. Produce documentation that future stories can use as the authoritative map of the application.
acceptanceCriteria: All major application routes/pages are identified and documented
All API routes and server-side integrations are identified
All external APIs/services are identified
Authentication and authorization flow is documented
Database and persistence layer are documented
AI integrations are documented
Course creation and learning flows are documented
Current LaTeX rendering implementation is identified
Important reusable UI components are identified
Critical user journeys are documented
No application functionality is removed during this discovery story
Documentation is committed to the repository

userStories.title: Inventory and verify every API integration
userStories.description: Test every API and external integration discovered during the application audit. Determine whether each integration works, fails, is deprecated, is unused, requires configuration, or needs replacement. Do not remove an integration merely because it is old or unfamiliar.
acceptanceCriteria: Every discovered API/integration has been tested where technically possible
Each API is classified as working, broken, deprecated, unused, configuration-dependent, or requiring replacement
HTTP/API responses and relevant failure reasons are recorded
Authentication and environment-variable requirements are documented without exposing secret values
API failures are investigated rather than silently ignored
Required broken APIs are identified for later repair
No existing API is silently deleted or replaced during the audit
An API audit document is created and committed

userStories.title: Fix required API and integration failures
userStories.description: Repair or replace API integrations that are required for the application and were identified as broken during the API audit. Preserve behavior where possible and document any unavoidable changes.
acceptanceCriteria: All critical broken integrations identified in the audit are repaired or replaced
Required API authentication/configuration works
Relevant application flows using the repaired integrations work
Deprecated integrations that require replacement are migrated where necessary
Unused integrations are not unnecessarily reintroduced
API audit documentation is updated with final status
Tests or verification evidence exist for repaired integrations
No secrets are committed

acceptanceCriteria: A consistent design system is established
Existing duplicated styling patterns are consolidated where practical
Typography is consistent
Spacing and layout conventions are consistent
Buttons and interactive controls are consistent
Forms and inputs are consistent
Cards and content containers are consistent
Loading, empty, and error states have reusable patterns
The design system supports responsive layouts
Existing functionality remains usable

userStories.title: Redesign the design system and color palette
userStories.description: Replace the current monochromatic cyan color palette with a modern, industry-standard design system. Establish a professional color palette with primary, secondary, accent, muted, destructive, and chart colors that provide visual variety and clear hierarchy. Update all design tokens, typography, spacing, and visual conventions to match modern SaaS application standards.
acceptanceCriteria: A new color palette with primary, secondary, accent, muted, destructive, and chart colors that are not all the same hue
CSS custom properties updated in globals.css for the full theme
shadcn components.json updated to reflect the new theme
Typography scale reviewed with clear visual hierarchy for headings, body, small text, and code
Spacing and radius tokens are consistent across the application
Border, ring, and focus colors match the new palette
Code block theming updated to match the new palette
Toast notifications use CSS variables instead of hardcoded hex values
The new theme is applied globally with no orphaned old-color references
The application has a cohesive, professional visual identity

userStories.title: Rebuild UI components to industry standard
userStories.description: Standardize all UI components across the application using shadcn/ui. Replace raw HTML elements with proper component library equivalents, consolidate icon libraries, improve course card visuals, and ensure every page uses consistent, accessible components that match the new design system.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing shadcn components installed where needed (Dialog, Select, Textarea, Tabs, Badge, Separator, Skeleton, Tooltip, Checkbox, Label)
All raw button elements replaced with shadcn Button
All raw input elements replaced with shadcn Input or Textarea where appropriate
window.confirm() calls replaced with AlertDialog component
alert() calls replaced with toast notifications or Dialog
Icon library consolidated to lucide-react throughout, react-icons removed
Emoji used as icons replaced with proper lucide icons
Course cards redesigned with improved visual treatment beyond letter initials
Loading states use Skeleton component where appropriate
All pages use consistent shadcn components
No custom button or input elements exist outside the shadcn system

userStories.title: Full page redesign per design system
userStories.description: Implement a complete redesign of all major application pages using the LEAP Neue design system (see .ralph/docs/ui-design-system.md for full palette, typography, spacing, component specs, and per-page wireframes). Pages to redesign: Dashboard/My Courses, Create Course (Basics + Stepper), Alter Roadmap editor, Choose Videos, Completed Courses (add back + redesign), and review the Learning/Course Player. Every page must use the design system tokens, shadcn components, lucide-react icons, responsive layout (sidebar collapses to mobile sheet), and follow the documented wireframes. This is the final visual transformation of the LEAP application.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard page redesigned per wireframe: header with logo+title+user, sidebar (mobile sheet), stats row, search + filter, course card grid using new Course Card spec
Create Course page redesigned per wireframe: 3-step stepper (Basics → Roadmap → Videos), card-based form with amber highlight on current step
Alter Roadmap editor redesigned per wireframe: draggable, collapsible chapter cards with inline subtopic editing, 'Generate with AI' button, save/commit bar
Choose Videos page redesigned per wireframe: search + selected-chip lane, tabbed filter (All/Selected), YouTube-style video grid with selection checkboxes, responsive grid columns
Completed Courses page recreated AND redesigned per wireframe: green badge, completion date, View Certificate + Share buttons; empty state when no courses
All pages use the LEAP Neue color palette, typography scale, radius tokens, and spacing grid from the design system
Every page has consistent Dashboard Header (logo, title, user button) and Sidebar with links to My Courses, Completed, Create Course, Upgrade
Sidebar collapses to hamburger menu + Sheet on mobile (md breakpoint)
All icons are lucide-react — no emoji, no react-icons, no raw SVGs
All cards, inputs, buttons, badges, and progress bars use shadcn components from components/ui/
Course cards follow the spec: thumbnail, title (2-line truncate), meta line, Progress bar, status Badge, 3-dot dropdown (MoreVertical) for Edit/Delete, hover lift
Empty and loading states use dedicated EmptyState / Skeleton components
react-hot-toast configured with CSS variables instead of hardcoded hex values
Dead files removed (Addcourse.jsx, components/LaTexRenderer.jsx, Features.jsx, Footer.jsx, Pricing.jsx, and any other zero-byte files)
Unused dependencies removed (react-icons, duplicate KaTeX packages, unused resend, unused @google/genai) after confirming no imports remain
Production build succeeds with zero new warnings and zero unused-import warnings
